checks: Compactness and limiting separating supports force a hypothetical far-away added point and P into the same old support face. Strict convexity reduces that face to P, giving the required locality without curvature assumptions.

The exterior ball at the lifted point intersects the cone to the old interior disk in positive-area sets on both sides of the vertical line. Hence both signature portions of the fill have strictly positive area.

A separately exposed point in the positive quadrant admits a fixed shallow cap away from P. Locality preserves its original trace. A continuous threshold shave removes the exact fill area and is disjoint from all three cut lines.

Since the apex is on the vertical line, any convex combination giving x=0 uses an old point on that same line. This proves the exact chord change and, together with signed areas, strict weight descent.
The original source §6 and frozen conclusion both optimize in the full class of convex bodies, so the segment formed by shaving is allowed.

overlap.comparison: Its polygon reduction fixes sector areas and rays and does not yield a descent step for an arbitrary strictly convex body.

readability: The statement and proof are readable as written.
review_method: Independent cold proof and archived-source review, with a separate exact symbolic or rational check where applicable.
summary: Strict convexity localizes the actual fill and makes the area-matched shave possible, with the local minimum conclusion in the full feasible class.
